cards.name: Stretch Master Control (edge)
cards.summary: A pseudo-effect (expression control container from PresetEffects.xml) holding a Transition Completion % slider and a '...the other side' checkbox for a legacy edge-stretch transition preset. On its own it renders nothing; it only drives expressions that read it.
use_for: only as the controller left behind by an old 'stretch from edge' transition preset
reading a 0-100 progress value from expressions when rebuilding such a transition by hand
avoid: applying it by match name and expecting a stretch: nothing changes on screen
no AE 2026 shipped preset uses it; use 'Transitions - Movement/Stretch - Edge.ffx' or 'Stretch Over - horizontal.ffx' instead

params.name: Transition Completion
params.does: transition progress in % read by the preset's expressions (0 = start, 100 = done)

params.name: ...the other side
params.does: checkbox (0/1): stretch from the opposite edge

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect (empty category, not in the Effects panel). Defined in Support Files/PresetEffects.xml; harvest shows NO AE 2026 preset uses it (the shipped 'Stretch - Edge.ffx' uses Slider Control + Transform). Adding it alone is a no-op: the visual comes from expressions on a Transform effect that read effect(...)('Transition Completion'). For an edge-stretch in-transition, apply the preset 'Transitions - Movement/Stretch - Edge.ffx' (or 'Stretch Over - horizontal/vertical.ffx') via layer.applyPreset instead. '...the other side' is a checkbox: 0/1.

verified.note: No frame: card status is 'hidden' (pseudo-effect controller that renders nothing without its preset expressions), so it was not rendered.

cards.name: Swarm
cards.summary: A pseudo-effect (expression control container) with Amplitude, Frequency and a Leader layer picker, meant for a 'swarm' behavior where layers jitter around a leader layer. It renders nothing by itself; the motion only exists if expressions read these controls.
use_for: controller for hand-written expressions that make icons / dots buzz around a leader null
insect / particle-like swarm of small graphic layers in an explainer
avoid: applying it alone: nothing moves
Leader is a layer reference and cannot be set from a spec

params.name: Amplitude
params.does: how far (px, assumed) followers wander from the leader

params.name: Frequency
params.does: wander speed in cycles per second (assumed)

params.name: Leader
params.does: layer the followers swarm around (layer reference)
params.typical: a null or the hero icon layer

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect defined in PresetEffects.xml next to Follow / Orbit 'DE' behavior controls; no AE 2026 preset in the harvest uses it (the 'Shapes/Backgrounds/Box Swarm.ffx' preset is unrelated). It is a no-op until expressions on Position read it, e.g. position = effect('Swarm')('Leader').transform.position + wiggle-style offset scaled by Amplitude/Frequency. Units of Amplitude/Frequency are inferred, not verified (low confidence). Leader is a layer param: a script must setValue(layerIndex) on it; 0 = none. Simpler route: write a wiggle() expression on Position parented to the leader.

verified.note: No frame: card status is 'hidden' (pseudo-effect controller that renders nothing without its preset expressions), so it was not rendered.

cards.name: Timer Controls
cards.summary: The control panel of the 'Text/Number Counters/Timer Countdown Monospaced' preset: an Animate Value slider plus formatting options that the preset's text expressions turn into a clock readout (MM:SS, HH:MM:SS or DD:HH:MM:SS) with optional unit labels. Alone, on a layer without the preset's expressions, it shows nothing.
use_for: countdown to a vote / result / deadline in a news reel
'time left' clock in an explainer or quiz
trailer countdown beat
elapsed-time readout over a documentary sequence
avoid: adding the effect without the preset: no text appears
renaming the effect instance: the preset's expressions look it up by its instance name 'Timer Countdown Controls'
entering seconds into Animate Value: the unit is minutes/hours/days depending on Time Format

params.name: Animate Value
params.does: the time shown, in the LARGEST unit of Time Format: minutes for MM:SS (1.5 = 01:30), hours for HH:MM:SS (default 9.9999 = 09:59:59), days for DD:HH:MM:SS; fraction = smaller units; sign ignored (Math.abs)
params.typical: MM:SS 10-s real-time countdown: keyframe 0.16667 -> 0 over 10 s (seconds / 60)

params.name: Time Format
params.does: dropdown: which clock fields are shown; also sets the unit of Animate Value

params.name: Show Labels
params.does: checkbox (0/1): show unit labels (Mins Secs ...) under the digits
params.typical: 1 for explainers, 0 for clean news graphics

params.name: Label Position Offset
params.does: x/y pixel offset of the label line

params.name: Label Size
params.does: label scale

params.name: Separator Character
params.does: dropdown: separator between fields

params.name: Spacing
params.does: extra spacing between digit groups

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect (labels from PresetEffects.xml). Do NOT add it by match name; apply the preset 'Text/Number Counters/Timer Countdown Monospaced.ffx' to a TEXT layer with layer.applyPreset, then find the effect by match name 'Pseudo/ADBE Timer Controls' (its instance is named 'Timer Countdown Controls'; expressions reference that name, so never rename it) and set/keyframe Animate Value. Verified from the preset's per-digit expression: Animate Value is in the largest unit of Time Format (MM:SS = minutes, HH:MM:SS = hours, DD:HH:MM:SS = days) and its fraction fills the smaller fields, so a 60-second countdown in MM:SS is 1 -> 0, NOT 60 -> 0 (60 would read 60:00). Keyframe linearly for a real-time clock. Default Time Format is 2 (HH:MM:SS): set it to 1 for short countdowns. Time Format / Separator are 1-based popups; Show Labels is 0/1. Use a monospaced-looking font for steady digits.

verified.note: No frame: card status is 'hidden' (pseudo-effect controller that renders nothing without its preset expressions), so it was not rendered.

cards.name: Trace Path
cards.summary: The control added by AE's 'Create Nulls From Paths' panel (Trace Path button): a Progress % slider and a Loop checkbox that drive a null along a mask or shape path (position via pointOnPath, rotation auto-oriented to the path tangent). Alone, without the generated expressions and a path, it does nothing.
use_for: move a pin / plane / car icon along a route on a map in an explainer
follow a drawn arrow path in a news graphic
parent a glow or text label to a null that traces a shape outline
avoid: adding it without a path and the generated null expression: no motion
needs a mask or shape path to trace

params.name: Progress
params.does: position along the path in % (0 = path start, 100 = path end)

params.name: Loop
params.does: checkbox (0/1, default 1): when on, the script's expression on Progress does loopOut('cycle') over its keyframes; without that expression it does nothing
params.typical: 0 for a one-off move along a route

cards.scripting: needs_input in practice: a mask or shape path. Hidden pseudo-effect added to a NEW NULL by Window > Create Nulls From Paths.jsx ('Trace Path' button; AE 2026 shows a deprecation note pointing to the native Layer > Create / Keyframe Assistant commands). The script keys Progress 0 -> 100 over 0-1 s, sets Loop on with a Progress expression that loopOut('cycle')s when Loop is on, sets null Position = pathLayer.toComp(pathToTrace.pointOnPath(progress)) and Rotation = atan2 of tangentOnPath(progress). To reproduce by script: add a null, add 'Pseudo/ADBE Trace Path', set Position expression var L = thisComp.layer('<path layer>'); L.toComp(L.mask(1).maskPath.pointOnPath(effect('Trace Path')('Progress')/100)) (toComp is required: pointOnPath returns layer space; use the shape group's Path property for shape layers). Set Loop 0 for a one-off move. Pair with Trim Paths End keyframed to the same timing to draw the route as the icon travels.

verified.note: No frame: card status is 'hidden' (pseudo-effect controller that renders nothing without its preset expressions), so it was not rendered.

avoid: adding it alone and expecting a transition

params.name: Transition Completion

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect from PresetEffects.xml; the harvest finds no AE 2026 preset using it (current presets use per-family controllers such as Slide / Stretch / Wipe / Fade / Dissolve Master Control). It is a no-op unless expressions read effect('Transition Master Control')('Transition Completion'). Useful as a single driver if a script writes such expressions; otherwise apply a 'Transitions - Movement/Dissolves/Wipes' preset.

cards.name: Wiggle - gelatin
cards.summary: Control panel of the 'Behaviors/Wiggle - gelatin' preset: speed and amount sliders that the preset's Transform-effect expressions use to wiggle Skew (by Wiggle Amount) while Skew Axis also wanders randomly (+/-180 deg), so the layer wobbles like jelly in changing directions. Scale is NOT touched. Added alone (without the preset) it does nothing.
use_for: playful jelly wobble on a sticker, emoji or logo in a reel
comic emphasis on a cut-out photo in a satire explainer
idle motion on an icon in an AI-education explainer
avoid: full-frame live action: the wobble looks cheap and distorts faces
large amounts make text unreadable
adding the bare effect: no motion without the preset's expressions

params.name: Wiggle Speed (wigs/sec)
params.does: wobbles per second (also the speed of the skew-axis drift)

params.name: Wiggle Amount
params.does: max Transform Skew around 0 (Skew units, capped at 70)

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect. Apply the preset 'Behaviors/Wiggle - gelatin.ffx' with layer.applyPreset: it adds a Transform effect whose Skew = wiggle(speed, Wiggle Amount) and Skew Axis = wiggle(speed, 180) (verified in the .ffx). Then set the sliders via the effect found by match name 'ADBE CM WiggleGelatin'. Adding only this match name is a no-op. Behavior runs continuously from the layer start; keyframe Wiggle Amount to 0 to stop it. For a fixed-direction lean use 'Wiggle - shear'; for a squash/stretch pulse use 'Wiggle - scale'.

verified.note: No frame: card status is 'hidden' (pseudo-effect controller that renders nothing without its preset expressions), so it was not rendered.

cards.name: Wiggle - position
cards.summary: Control panel of the 'Behaviors/Wiggle - position' preset: speed and pixel-amount sliders that the preset's Transform-effect expressions use to jitter the layer's position randomly (a handheld / floating drift). Alone it does nothing.
use_for: subtle handheld float on a still photo in a documentary
camera-shake hit on an impact beat in a trailer (high speed, brief)
gentle drift on lower-thirds or stickers in reels
avoid: big amounts on full-frame footage reveal the frame edge: scale the layer up ~105-110% first
adding the bare effect: no motion without the preset

params.name: Wiggle Speed (wigs/sec)
params.does: random moves per second
params.typical: 0.5-2 for a float, 8-15 for a shake hit

params.name: Wiggle Amount (pixels)
params.does: max offset in pixels

cards.equivalent: Transform (keyframed Position) - Premiere has no built-in wiggle
cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect. Apply 'Behaviors/Wiggle - position.ffx' with layer.applyPreset (adds Transform + this control with wiggle expressions), then set sliders on the effect with match name 'ADBE CM WigglePosition'. Adding this effect alone is a no-op. Equivalent hand route: expression wiggle(freq, amp) on Position. For a shake hit, keyframe Wiggle Amount (pixels) up then down.

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect. Apply 'Behaviors/Wiggle - shear.ffx' via layer.applyPreset (adds a Transform effect whose Skew = wiggle(speed, Wiggle Amount); Skew Axis is not animated, verified in the .ffx), then set sliders on match name 'ADBE CM WiggleShear'. Alone it is a no-op. Do not stack with 'Wiggle - gelatin': both drive Skew on their own Transform effects.

cards.summary: Control panel of the 'Behaviors/Wigglerama' preset: one panel that wiggles position, rotation and scale together (with a nervousness/octaves control) through the preset's Transform-effect expressions, giving an all-round random float or shake. Alone it does nothing.
use_for: organic handheld float on stills / screenshots in a documentary
camera-shake hit on a trailer impact (high speed, short)
lively idle motion on stickers and lower-thirds in reels
avoid: full-frame footage without scaling up shows frame edges
high nervousness + big amounts looks chaotic, not cinematic
adding the bare effect: no motion without the preset

cards.scripting: Hidden pseudo-effect. Apply 'Behaviors/Wigglerama.ffx' via layer.applyPreset (adds Transform + this control), then set sliders on match name 'ADBE CM Wigglerama'. Defaults (25 px, 30 deg, 15 %) are far too strong for live action: lower rotation to ~2 and scale to ~3 for a handheld float. Checkbox is 0/1. Alone it is a no-op.
